messages:
cs_jordan: ⚠️ Customer esk: multiple 5xx and gateway timeouts hitting /v1/generate in eu-west-1 between 09:12-09:38 UTC. They attached sample trace ids. They say retries don't help, big impact on live traffic. Can SRE triage?

oncall_lee: seeing it too, started drilldown. Frontend gateway logs show lots of 504s and 502s during scale-up windows. Looks correlated with pod creation spikes and readiness delays.

zack_sre: copying initial logs for one trace id -> trace: df3a9c. Gateway stack: envoy -> ingress-nginx -> inference-svc. Envoy timings: upstream connect timed out. Nginx: 504 while waiting for response from upstream.

zack_sre: KEDA/HPA events around same time:
```
ScaledObject events: scale to 0 -> scale to 5 requested (target 80% cpu).
HPA events: no scale because metrics server returning stale values.
Pods created: 5, but readiness probes failing (app not responding on /health) for ~25-40s each.
```

marta_devex: that aligns with customer report: they saw initial fast failures, then a bunch of successful attempts after ~45s. Could be cold start + model warmup. Which model? gpt-medium-ocq (open quantized). Warmup usually ~30s on p4d for that model.

cs_jordan: paste of customer repro curl (anonymized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "X-Request-ID: df3a9c" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium-ocq","input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.eu-west-1.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response: 504 gateway timeout.

zack_sre: config relevant: KEDA ScaledObject had `minReplicaCount: 0`, `cooldownPeriod: 300` (5m), and `pollingInterval: 30`. HPA has `behavior` with `scaleDown` stabilization window 300s and `scaleUp` limited via `percent` policies. We also rolled a minor autoscaler config change 2 hours before incident (PR #4426) that adjusted HPA stabilization to avoid flapping.

oncall_lee: hypothesis: scale-to-zero + aggressive HPA stabilization + long readiness/warmup => bursts of traffic hit zero pods, KEDA triggers scale-up but HPA/stabilization/cooldown prevent replicas from being usable quickly, causing gateway 5xx/timeouts. Readiness probe timing means pods aren't available until model loaded.

dakota_prod: we need to verify metrics server staleness claim. I see in cluster-monitoring that metrics-server had intermittent timeouts at 09:10-09:15 (short spike). That could explain HPA not seeing actual demand until later, delaying scale.

marta_devex: customers with strict latency SLAs will always hit this if we scale to zero. Options: pre-warm, increase minReplicaCount for critical routes, or use warmup hooks in readiness probe to report ready earlier while model warms (but that risks returning 503s).

zack_sre: quick repro steps I used locally against staging: 1) set minReplicaCount=0 for target deployment 2) send 50 concurrent requests -> observe 50x 504s for ~25s while pods spin and warm. I can paste raw pod logs showing model loader:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:32Z model-loader INFO loading weights
2026-03-15T09:12:46Z runtime INFO aten conv kernel compiled
2026-03-15T09:12:58Z model-loader INFO kv cache warmup complete
2026-03-15T09:13:00Z readiness probe failed: /health not responding
2026-03-15T09:13:20Z readiness probe success
```

cs_jordan: customer also included cost concern — they prefer scale-to-zero but SLA requires occasional warm capacity.

oncall_lee: immediate mitigation implemented at 09:22: changed scaledobject for eu-west-1 critical route: `minReplicaCount: 2` and reduced `cooldownPeriod` to 60s. Also increased HPA `scaleUp` policy to allow faster percent growth. I've triggered a rolling restart to reconcile.

ops-bot: Deploy event: autoscaler-config update applied by oncall_lee at 2026-03-15T09:22:10Z (sha: a1b2c3d).

zack_sre: after change, saw successful handling of burst at 09:27: error rate dropped to baseline, latency stabilized. We'll monitor for 1h.

marta_devex: long term suggestions:
- introduce proactive pre-warm for high-priority customers (scheduled warm pools)
- provide per-route SLO config so customers can opt-out of scale-to-zero
- add a warmup readiness lifecycle: respond `readiness: true` sooner and return `202 Accepted` while model still loading with a short-circuiting gateway that queues/buffers instead of 504
- reduce metric staleness by adding fallback metrics from sidecar (local cpu/mem) for HPA decisions

dakota_prod: action items created: INC-2026-184 (increase minReplica default for critical pools), TASK-PR#4460 (add sidecar metric exporter for HPA), RFC-88 (warmup lifecycle + API semantics). Assigned to zack_sre / marta_devex.

cs_jordan: customer updated: we told them a mitigation (minReplica change) and ETA for durable solution (postmortem + opt-in prewarm). They're moderate satisfied for now but will escalate if it reoccurs.

zack_sre: preliminary root cause: combination of scale-to-zero (minReplicaCount=0), KEDA polling/scale cooldown, HPA stabilization window, and model warmup time (25-40s). Metrics-server flakiness amplified delay. Rolling config change earlier that tightened stabilization unintentionally slowed scale-up responsiveness.

oncall_lee: tagging postmortem and scheduling blameless review tomorrow 10:00 UTC. If anyone has more logs/traces, drop them here.

cs_jordan: thanks all. Closing incident channel once postmortem link posted.
